topics.label: Introduction to cancer therapy
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the session's learning objectives and frames the overview of cancer therapy approaches.

topics.label: Conventional cancer therapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine traditional modalities of cancer treatment, including surgical resection, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic chemotherapy, alongside their mechanisms and limitations.

topics.label: Exploiting cellular vulnerabilities and repair defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss therapeutic strategies that target intrinsic vulnerabilities of cancer cells, including hormone signaling dependence, checkpoint alterations, and DNA repair deficiencies.

topics.label: Kinase-targeted therapies and resistance mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics cover the application of small-molecule kinase inhibitors against oncogene-addicted cancers and the molecular mechanisms underlying resistance and drug addiction.

topics.label: Monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how engineered monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates are used to target tumor surface markers and deliver cytotoxic payloads.

topics.label: Cancer immunotherapy and immune surveillance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the biological basis of cancer immune surveillance and modern immunotherapeutic approaches that harness T cells to attack tumor cells.

topics.label: Challenges, historical trends, and future directions in cancer treatment
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate broader clinical challenges, historical survival outcomes, genomic patient stratification, and ethical considerations in managing cancer.
